Introduction to
Nursing Management During 
Pregnancy

Risk Factors for Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes
 Isotretinoins- Accutane for acne 
treatment
 Alcohol misuse-No safe levels 
established. Fetal Alcohol 
Syndrome FAS-effects 
neurological development of fetus 
 Anti-epileptic drugs-Valproic Acid 
(Depakote) is a teratogen
 Diabetes (preconception) 3X 
increase in birth defects.
 Folic acid deficiency-decrease 
neural tube
 STI-testing at 1st visit/36 wks, 
treatment and protection during 
pregnancy
 HIV/AIDS-Testing pre-concept. 
Treatment during pregnancy/labor 
to reduce transmission
 Hypothyroidism-Levothyroxine 
dosage may need to be adjusted 
pregnancy 
 Maternal phenylketonurea-women 
with PKU  e abnormalities on low 
phenylalanine diet.
 Rubella sero-negativity
 Obesity-pregnancy not a time for 
dieting. Optimal weight before 
pregancy
 Oral anticoagulant-coumadin is a 
teratogen.  Change to heparin for 
pregnancy
  Smoking-affects birth weight.  
LBW and pre-term pregnancies 
associated with smoking

Preconception Care
 Immunization status
 Any underlying medical conditions-5% of women have some history
 Reproductive health care practices
 Sexuality and sexual practices
 Nutrition-history and preferences
 Lifestyle practices
 Psychosocial issues 
 Medication and drug use-3 % are taking a teratogenic substance
 Support system-who will be there during and after

Comprehensive Health History  
 Reason for seeking care
 Suspicion of pregnancy
 Date of last menstrual period LMP
 Signs and symptoms of pregnancy
 Urine or blood test for hCG
 Past medical, surgical, and personal history 
 Woman’s reproductive history: menstrual, obstetric, and 
gynecologic history

Menstrual History
 Menstrual cycle
 Age at menarche
 Days in cycle
 Flow characteristics: Heavy vs light
 Discomforts: PMS, cramps, 
 Use of contraception: plan for post-pregnancy

Menstrual History: Calculating EDD
 Date of last menstrual period (LMP)
 Calculation of estimated or expected date of birth (EDB) or delivery 
(EDD)
 Naegele’s rule
 Use first day of LMP        11/21/25
 Subtract 3 months            8/21/25
 Add 7 days                     8/28/25
 Add 1 year                   8/28/26 = EDD
 Gestational or birth calculator or wheel
 Apps abound to calculate EDD/EDB
 Ultrasound is best method of dating a pregnancy-most accurate for 
dating- Here’s the accuracy
 ±5 days @ 8 weeks
 ±10 days @ 18 weeks
 ±15 days @ 28 weeks

Naegele’s Rule
 Calculating the EDD by the following formula:
 FIRST DAY OF LMP Aug 20 th 2025
- 3MONTHS May 20th 2025
+ 7 DAYS May 27th 2025
 T+ 1 YEAR Aug  20th 2026
 This date is approximately 280 days (40 weeks) from the 
LMP.

6
Term
 Term: beginning of week 38 of gestation to end of week 
42 of gestation
 Preterm: Less than 37weeks and 6/7days 
 Extremely preterm <28 wks
 Very preterm 28-32 wks
 Late preterm between 34 0/7 and 37 6/7 wks
 Post-term >42+ wks 
 Post-dates >40 wks
 Viability: capacity to live outside uterus; about 22 to 24 
weeks since last menstrual period, or fetal weight 
greater than 500 g
5

Physical Examination
 Vital signs
 Head-to-toe assessment
 Head and neck
 Chest
 Abdomen, including fundal height if appropriate
 Extremities
 Pelvic examination
 Examination of external and internal genitalia
 Bimanual examination
 Estimation of pelvic shape  by provider
 Gynecoid shape most common (most favorable for delivery)
Physical Examination

Routine Prenatal Tests and Why 
 Urinalysis/urine dip: Beginning in the 2nd trimester (or earlier if risk factors exist)
 Glucose: Gestational diabetes screening
 Protein: Preeclampsia is diagnosed by presence of protein in urine with elevated B/P
 Leukocytes: Presence of WBCs in urine indicator of UTI (associated with pre-term labor)
 Nitrites: Bacteria breakdown nitrates into nitrites indicator of UTI 
 Complete blood count: 
 Pregnancy increases blood volume by 30-50% (50% increase plasma & 20% increase RBCs)
 Due to increase in plasma volume, there is mild dilutional anemia (10-11g/dL is normal)
 Blood typing & Rh factor: Rh- mother with Rh+ infant can produce antibodies that can 
cause hemolysis in newborn = hyperbilirubinemia in infant. 
 Rubella titer (if non-immune = vaccine AFTER pregnancy)
 Rubella can cause severe congenital defects or death in fetus
 All women of child-bearing age should know their status and get vaccinated if not immune
 Hepatitis B surface antigen (+ HBsAG = active or chronic Hep B infection)
 Infant can contract during delivery 
 Within 12 hours of birth Hep B Immunoglobulin (HBIG)  & Hep B vaccine must be given. Followed 
by regular 1 month and 6 months
 Repeat infant testing for Hep B @ 9 & 15 months to check for immunity

Routine Prenatal Tests and Why Cont.
 HIV: Transmittable during pregnancy, birth and breastfeeding
 HIV+ patients who take antiretroviral therapy ART with undetectable viral load have less 
than 1% chance of transmission.  
 HIV+ patients will receive IV ART in labor to further reduce any risk
 Rapid Plasma Reagin (RPR) testing- Syphilis antibody
 Must be confirmed with Treponema pallidum particle agglutination assay (TP-
PA) Fluorescent treponemal antibody absorption (FTA-ABS) test
 Cervical smears-STI testing
 Chlamydia, gonorrhea: Transmission during delivery can have profound effect 
on newborn (eye infections, pneumonia, sepsis)
 Group Beta Strep: NOT AN INFECTION, Normal flora on perineum of some 
women.  
 Transmission occurs during birth; respiratory infection, sepsis, meningitis of neonate 
 Treated by IV antibiotics during labor at least 4 hours before birth, given every 4 hrs until 
delivery to reduce # of bacteria on perineum to prevent (e.g. Ampicillin 2g loading dose, 
then 1g IV every 4 hours)
 Ultrasound(s)
 Dating 11-14 weeks: Most accurate dating becomes less accurate later wks
 Anatomy Scan 18-22 weeks: All organ systems formed 
 Growth Scan: Monitor development and track growth (maybe)
 Additional Scans: If needed to monitor fetal well-being

Follow-up Visits
 Visit schedule: 
 Every 4 weeks up to 28 weeks
 1st trimester ultrasound
 Fetal anatomy scan
 Amniocentesis if needed
 Gestational Diabetes screening @ 24-26 weeks
 Every 2 weeks from 29 to 36 weeks
 Weekly until birth

Follow-up Visits (cont’d.)
 Assessments
 Weight & BP compared to baseline values
 Urine testing for protein, glucose, ketones, and nitrites
 Fundal height: 12-14 weeks fundus rises above symphysis pubis
 Reaches umbilicus at approx 20 wks measures 20cm.
 Fundus is measured at each visit beginning at 20 wks from pubic 
symphysis to top of fundus= cms = wks gestation
 Measuring small (dating, fetal growth restriction, anomalies)
 Measuring large (dating, GDM, polyhydramnios [too much fluid]
 Quickening/fetal movement
 Fetal heart rate assessment via doppler
 Electronic Fetal Monitoring on L& D unit
 Teaching: danger signs

Call Immediately if…
1st Trimester
Vaginal bleeding or spotting-miscarriage
Hyperemesis gravidarum-persistant vomiting
Fever > 100. ° F (37.7°C)
Lower abdominal or shoulder pain
2nd Trimester-everything above AND
Regular uterine contractions- pre-term labor
Calf pain-DVT
Gush or leakage of fluid from vagina
Absence of fetal movement for more than 12 hours
3rd Trimester-everything above AND
Sudden weight gain > 2kg in 1 week
Peri-orbital or facial edema
Severe upper abdominal or epigastric pain
Headache with visual changes-pregnancy induced HTN
Decrease in fetal movements

Fetal Well-being and Movement
Maternal perception of fetal movements is a non-invasive 
indicator of fetal well-being (at about 28 weeks)
 Should be done at same time each day
 Random: Lie or sit and concentrate on fetal movements
 Count should = 10 movements within 1 hour
 If not able to feel as above: Have a snack or juice
 Lie on left side for 1 hour after, concentrate
 Count should = 10 movements in 1 hour
 May repeat for 2nd hour, if longer than 2 hours= call provider
Deviation from normal fetal movement should be reported to 
health care provider.

Fundal Height Measurement
 Fundus = 20 cm above pubic symphysis (umbilicus) @ 
20 weeks
 Fundus cm measurement = weeks pregnant until 36 
wks
 34 wks = 34 cms
 Fundal height may return to 36 cms as engagement 
occurs (fetus moves into pelvis at end of term)
 Engagement: Fetus “drops”

1st Trimester Discomforts
 Urinary frequency or incontinence 
 Fatigue-hormonal changes, oxygen demands, metabolic demands
 Nausea and vomiting-hCG & estrogen levels increase
 High protein snack before bed, rise slowly, ginger or ginger ale
 Avoid fried or highly fatty food, avoid strong smells highly seasoned 
foods
 Breast tenderness-hormonal changes
 Constipation-progesterone-decreases peristalsis
 Nasal stuffiness, bleeding gums, epistaxis
 Cravings
 Leukorrhea

2nd Trimester Discomforts
Some 1st trimester comforts continue and:
 Backache-lie on left side, pillow between legs
 Low heels
 Varicosities of the vulva and legs-support 
stockings, stool softeners, fluid intake
 Hemorrhoids-avoid constipation: stool softeners, 
increase fluid intake, fiber rich foods, sitz-baths, 
witch hazel, hemorrhoid creams 
 Flatulence with bloating-avoid trigger foods beans, 
cabbage, white sugar.  Increase fluid intake.

3rd Trimester Discomforts
 Return of 1st trimester discomforts: fatigue, breast 
tenderness, urinary frequency, leukorrhea, 
constipation
 Increase fluid intake, loose fitting clothing, rest, small 
frequent meals. Avoid spicy/high fat foods
 Shortness of breath and dyspnea: Fetus presses 
upward.  Elevate HOB.  Avoid over heating.  May 
resolve with lightening. Drop of fetus into pelvis in 
preparation for birth.
 Heartburn and indigestion- Remain upright after 
meals. TUMS TUMS TUMS
 Avoid trigger foods, caffeine, chocolate, eat small frequent 
meals.

Discomforts of 3rd Trimester Cont
 Dependent edema
 Supportive stockings 
 Elevate feet (above heart) 
 Lie on left side
 Increase fluid intake
 Braxton Hicks contractions
 Irregular painless uterine contractions that don’t cause 
cervical dilation
 Do not increase with walking
 Keep hydrated

Nursing Management to Promote Self-Care
 Personal hygiene-may perspire more or perspiration 
may have more odor
 Avoidance of saunas and hot tubs-May cause fetal 
tachycardia and expose mother to bacteria
 Perineal care-No douching.  No panty liners
 Loose fitting cotton underwear
 Dental care- Dentist before pregnancy, soft brush
 Breast care-comfortable and supportive bra 
 Clothing-Loose layered, Low-heeled shoes
 Exercise: continue all activities as tolerated
 Moderate exercise routine can be started
 Walking, swimming, yoga

Nursing Management to Promote Self-Care 
(cont’d.) 
 Sleep and rest-regular schedule
 Avoid lying on back.
 pressure on inferior vena cava-decreases blood return
 Exercise: for uncomplicated pregnancies
 Walking, swimming, low-impact activities
 Can continue regular routine
 Sexual activity and sexuality-normal sexual activity is safe and 
healthy
 Avoid intercourse if vaginal bleeding, pre-term contractions, 
rupture of membranes, diagnosed with cervical insufficiency
 Normal cervix > 3.0 cm risk for PTL
 Employment
 Appropriate rest/breaks. 
 Travel- 3 point seatbelt, across chest and under belly, sit further 
back from steering wheel

Immunizations and medications
Vaccines That Should Be Considered Unless Contraindicated (ACOG, 2024)
• Hepatitis B
• Influenza (inactivated) injection Every Pregnancy During Flu Season
• Tetanus/diphtheria (Tdap) Every Pregnancy
  Covid 19 (No data supports pregnancy problems)
Vaccines Contraindicated during Pregnancy
• Influenza (live, attenuated vaccine) nasal spray
• Measles
• Mumps
• Rubella
• Varicella
• BCG (tuberculosis)
• Typhoid

Preparation for Labor, Birth, and Parenthood
 Perinatal education
 Childbirth education
 Lamaze (psychoprophylactic) method: focus on breathing 
and relaxation techniques
 Bradley (partner-coached childbirth) method: focus on 
exercises and slow, controlled abdominal breathing
 Dick-Read (natural childbirth) method: focus on fear 
reduction via knowledge and abdominal breathing 
techniques

Preparation for Labor, Birth, and Parenthood 
(cont’d.) 
 Feeding choices
 Breast-feeding: advantages and disadvantages
 Bottle feeding: advantages and disadvantages
 Teaching 
 Final preparation for labor and birth
 Contact information
 Pack bag
 Birth plan- what do you want?

Additional Prenatal Testing/Intervention
 18 – 20 wks:  second trimester sonogram
 24 – 28 wks:  glucose tolerance test
 28 -- 30 wks: RhoGam if indicated
 34 wks:  rpt CBC
 36 + wks:  group B strep
 Amniocentisis after 34 weeks for fetal lung maturity

Gestational Diabetes Screening 
 24-28 weeks is most accurate
 1st trimester screening for high risk
 Obesity
 History of gestational diabetes
 Family history of diabetes
 Oral 50gm glucose drink, plasma glucose 1 hour later
Result of ≥130 mg/dL = follow-up testing needed
 Follow-up test: 3 hr testing
 Fasting glucose: 100gm glucose drink followed by 3 serum draws 
at 1 hour intervals. Normal Results:
Fasting =  95 mg/dL≦
1 hour  180 mg/dL≦
2 hour  155 mg/dL≦
3 hour  140 mg/dL≦

Variations in Prenatal Care—cont’d 
 Age differences
 Adolescents
 Much less likely than older women to receive 
adequate prenatal care
 Women older than 35 years 
 Multiparous women
 Nulliparous women
